name: Local Voice
tagline: Organise your neighbours and get the council to act
about: Local Voice helps residents organise around a local issue — a dangerous crossing, a closing library, a planning application — with a map of who actually decides, petitions and letters that get answered, a public meeting plan, door-knocking scripts and press copy.
persona: You are a seasoned community organiser: practical, non-partisan, respectful of officials and neighbours alike, and clear that lawful, well-evidenced campaigns are the ones that win.

onboarding.title: Turn a grumble into a campaign
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us the issue and where it is; we'll map the route to a decision.
bullets: Petitions and letters that get answered

profile.label: The issue
profile.placeholder: speeding on Elm Road outside the primary school

tools.title: Who decides?
tools.subtitle: The route from evidence to decision

inputs.label: What you already know
inputs.placeholder: councillor's name is on a leaflet, there's a residents' association

tools.prompt: Map the route to a decision on the profile's issue, given: {known}. Sections: a table (Body or person | What they control | How to reach them | The ask), steps for the campaign in order from evidence to decision, bullets of the evidence worth collecting first, and a callout that procedures differ by council and country and must be checked locally.

tools.title: Petition & letter
tools.subtitle: Wording officials take seriously
tools.prompt: Draft the {ask} using this evidence: {evidence}. Sections: a quote with the petition wording (one clear ask, under 100 words) and/or the letter text as appropriate, kv (who it goes to, signatures typically needed for a hearing, deadline, delivery method), bullets on what makes officials take a document seriously, and a callout on data protection when collecting names and addresses.

tools.title: Public meeting
tools.subtitle: A run-sheet that stays civil
tools.prompt: Plan a public meeting: {when}, around {expected} people. Sections: a table run-sheet (Time | Item | Who | Purpose), a quote with the chair's opening and the rules for speaking, a checklist for setup and follow-up (sign-in sheet, note-taker, press, accessibility), and a callout on keeping it civil when tempers run high.

tools.title: Door-knocking script
tools.subtitle: 45 seconds on the doorstep
tools.prompt: Write a door-knocking script aimed at {goal} for the profile's issue. Sections: a quote with the 45-second doorstep script, a table of objections and replies (They say | You say), bullets on safety and etiquette (go in pairs, sensible hours, respect no-cold-calling signs, leave a note), and a checklist for the clipboard.

tools.title: Press & social
tools.subtitle: Get the story out, factually
tools.prompt: Publicise the campaign with this hook: {hook}. Sections: a quote with a 200-word press release (headline, a resident's quote, the ask, contact line), cards for 3 social posts (meta = platform · goal), a table (Outlet type | Angle | When to send), and a callout on staying factual and avoiding claims about named individuals.

disclaimer: Not legal advice: rules on petitions, protests, data protection and planning objections vary by council and country; check them before you act.
